## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.

-   Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.

-   Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.

-   Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.

-   Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
-   Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
-   Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
-   Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
-   Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To explore broader distribution, the team proposes a hypothetical partnership with a digital art marketplace or a journalism organization to integrate the tool and provide it directly to their communities of creators.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of future planning, exploring integration pathways with potential partner platforms is proposed.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access.

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly.

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team. The team is open to exploring potential future partnerships with organizations that share a mission to protect digital authenticity.

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. Future plans could include exploring distribution through partner channels.

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
-   Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
-   Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
-   Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
-   Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test with its defined goal, and to execute the proposed public demonstration.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development.

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability

To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, and to execute the proposed public demonstration.

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability

To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with subscription options for higher-volume users. As hypothetical examples to make this tangible, proposed pricing tiers could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited,' and an annual payment option could be considered, such as '$50 per year for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, and to execute the proposed public demonstration.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development and the proposed pricing model.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust. To help visualize the solution for this segment, the team proposes to include a mock-up or wireframe screenshot of the proposed beta interface tailored for digital illustrators in the project description.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability

To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, to execute the proposed public demonstration, and to create the proposed interface mock-up or wireframe. To make the use of funds more tangible, a simple, hypothetical percentage breakdown could be: 50% for development (hiring and engineering), 30% for design and user experience, and 20% for testing, infrastructure, and initial operational costs.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development and the proposed pricing model.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta, planned for the month following successful funding. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust, planned for the third week of the campaign. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status
The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta, planned for the month following successful funding. A proposed, clear metric for the success of this test is the percentage of test users who successfully completed the fingerprinting workflow without assistance, with a target of 100% completion without assistance. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust, planned for the third week of the campaign. To help visualize the solution for this segment, the team proposes to include a mock-up or wireframe screenshot of the proposed beta interface tailored for digital illustrators in the project description.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability
To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, to execute the proposed public demonstration, and to create the proposed interface mock-up or wireframe.

## Risks & Challenges
The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships
The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details
Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development and the proposed pricing model.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem
The digital landscape is saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. The central question is how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on. To make the value proposition more tangible, consider a hypothetical example: a digital illustrator could use the tool to generate a fingerprint of their new artwork file before posting it on the named social platform. Later, if a copy appears elsewhere, the illustrator can publicly prove they had the original file first by showing the time-stamped ledger entry matching their file's fingerprint, without ever revealing the full file.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
- Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
- Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
- Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
- Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets. To focus the initial beta launch, the team proposes concentrating development and marketing efforts on a specific, narrow user segment. The proposed initial target is digital illustrators who primarily share their work on a single, major social media platform.

## Development Status
The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule. As part of this plan, the team proposes to tailor the initial beta interface and user experience specifically for the needs and workflows of the proposed target segment of digital illustrators. To help visualize the solution for this segment, the team proposes to include a mock-up or wireframe screenshot of the proposed beta interface tailored for digital illustrators in the project description. To inform this tailoring, the team proposes a small-scale, planned test with a handful of digital illustrators from the target platform to gather initial workflow feedback before the beta, planned for the month following successful funding. This test is proposed to involve a clear, simple metric of 5 test users to show structured planning and manageability. A proposed, clear metric for the success of this test is the percentage of test users who successfully completed the fingerprinting workflow without assistance. Furthermore, the team proposes a planned, small-scale public demonstration of the technology's verification capability using a sample file to be conducted during the crowdfunding campaign to build trust, planned for the third week of the campaign.

## Revenue Model and Sustainability
To address a key backer question about long-term viability, the team is considering a proposed, simple pricing structure. This could take the form of a freemium model, for example, offering a limited number of free verifications per month with a subscription option for higher-volume users. As a hypothetical example to make this tangible, a proposed pricing tier could be '5 free verifications per month, then $5 per month for unlimited.' The final model would be developed based on feedback from the initial beta and the proposed small-scale test.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access. This includes proposed work to adapt the initial product for the specific segment, to conduct the proposed small-scale test, to execute the proposed public demonstration, and to create the proposed interface mock-up or wireframe.

## Risks & Challenges
The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly. Focusing on a narrow initial segment is a proposed strategy to manage scope and accelerate learning.

## Team & Partnerships
The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details
Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact. To enhance credibility and transparency, the team proposes to anchor fingerprints to a specific public ledger technology, such as a public timestamping service like OpenTimestamps or a specific, energy-efficient blockchain.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets. The plan is to gather feedback from the initial, focused user segment, informed by the proposed small-scale test, to inform broader development and the proposed pricing model.

text_key: ## One-Sentence Summary A line of heirloom jewelry uses real leather that is cultivated in bioreactors from a one-time, harmless skin-cell sample taken from a living, sanctuary-grazing cow, aiming to offer animal-friendly leather adornments. ## Problem The creators frame conventional leather as dependent on animal harm and present a gap for ethically sourced, real leather that preserves the material's qualities without sacrificing animal welfare. ## One-Sentence Summary

A line of heirloom jewelry uses real leather that is cultivated in bioreactors from a one-time, harmless skin-cell sample taken from a living, sanctuary-grazing cow, aiming to offer animal-friendly leather adornments.

## Problem

The creators frame conventional leather as dependent on animal harm and present a gap for ethically sourced, real leather that preserves the material's qualities without sacrificing animal welfare. They position the project as evidence that leather can be made while the donor animal continues to live and be cared for at a sanctuary.

## Solution / Product Overview

The project offers jewelry featuring inlays of cultivated leather grown from the donor cow's skin cells on a plant-based scaffold. The leather is produced in bioreactors and then vegetable-tanned, allowing the creators to present finished wearable pieces while asserting that no additional animal harvesting is required.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Real leather cultivated from living-animal skin cells grown on a plant-derived scaffold.

-   Inlays set within metal bezels and protected under a glass dome cabochon.

-   Options to choose hypoallergenic stainless steel or sterling silver for certain pieces.

-   Offered in multiple size, color, and material combinations.

-   Packaged in eco-friendly boxes cushioned with plant seed fiber used in the cultivation process.

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign speaks to people seeking animal-friendly, sustainable jewelry and those interested in owning a first-of-its-kind heirloom piece made from cultivated leather grown from a specific donor animal's cells.

## Development Status

The team shows finished jewelry inlays and describes past milestones: cells were isolated harmlessly in 2023, prototypes include a pendant and a card holder made in early 2025, and the leather is grown with patent-pending plant-based scaffolding. They state there are no outside approvals required and that the technology and cell lines are owned by the creators.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned actions include pilot testing to tune color and texture, inspecting scaffold density before use, preparing different concentrations of plant-based tanning ingredients, and securing jewelry settings after style counts are finalized at the end of the campaign. Production scaling will be addressed by adjusting modular cultivated-leather bioreactor technology and resources.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds support bringing the cultivated-leather jewelry to backers: producing inlays, performing pilot tests for consistency, and procuring jewelry settings and sustainable packaging to deliver finished pieces.

## Risks & Challenges

Stated risks include: loss of cryopreserved cells (mitigated by storage at multiple facilities); variability in final color and surface texture from vegetable tanning and scaffold differences (addressed through pilot testing and scaffold inspection); potential supply-chain changes requiring alternate jewelry settings of equal or better quality; and possible extended delivery times for later backers if demand is high.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by a founder with long-term tissue-engineering experience and cellular-agriculture leadership since 2018, who worked with a sanctuary and veterinary professionals to isolate the donor cells.

## What's Included

Jewelry pieces with cultivated-leather inlays (e.g., a rectangular inlay approximately 10 mm × 50 mm) and, for some items, a waxed linen cord; components are housed in metal bezels and glass cabochons.

## Technical Details

-   Plant-based scaffold from kapok seed fibers, needle-felted.

-   Surface treatment with plant-derived ingredients (e.g., sunflower lecithin, zein protein) to promote cell attachment.

-   Cells produce collagen that becomes vegetable-tanned leather.

-   Approximate inlay dimension: 10 mm × 50 mm.

The project proposes a simple path to participation: sponsor a hive through the app and receive honey harvested from that hive. -   Sponsor packages for individuals, families, schools, and businesses.

-   Professional placement and maintenance of hives in suitable habitats such as farms, gardens, and meadows.

-   Regular updates about the hive, including photos, videos, and reports on health and production.

-   Honey yields tied to sponsorship level, ranging from seasonal honey to curated gift boxes.

-   Educational materials and opportunities to visit a hive under expert guidance.

-   App roadmap features including an activity-tracking dashboard with visual data and a feedback system.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Eco-conscious individuals, families, schools, companies, and local farmers seeking direct support for pollination, educational engagement, or corporate sustainability initiatives are explicitly referenced.

## Development Status

The team plans to develop a minimum viable technology platform and initial branding while assembling beekeeper partnerships; the page does not claim a finished product.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

-   Phase 1 (0--6 months): establish beekeeper/apiary partnerships in one state, build an MVP platform, and create initial marketing.

-   Phase 2 (6--12 months): enhance the platform with an activity dashboard, add a feedback system, and expand the beekeeper network.

-   Phase 3 (12--18 months): expand to a multi-state region, introduce premium offerings, and launch a corporate program. Additionally, the team aims to deploy hundreds of hives across the region by 2026.

Funds will support hive placement and maintenance, technology development, beekeeper partnerships, creation of new bee habitats, research on bee health, education in schools and communities, and sustainable beekeeping practices.

The campaign lists regulatory/permit timing, high winter mortality (about 40%), pesticide exposure, limited forage, and climate-driven bloom variability causing 20--50% yield fluctuations as key risks.

Ongoing communications include regular hive updates and, as the platform evolves, an activity dashboard and feedback mechanisms; the team also plans educational programming and a corporate offering.

## One-Sentence Summary

A line of heirloom jewelry uses real leather that is cultivated in bioreactors from a one-time, harmless skin-cell sample taken from a living, sanctuary-grazing cow, aiming to offer animal-friendly leather adornments.

## Problem

The creators frame conventional leather as dependent on animal harm and present a gap for ethically sourced, real leather that preserves the material's qualities without sacrificing animal welfare. They position the project as evidence that leather can be made while the donor animal continues to live and be cared for at a sanctuary. The project also addresses the challenge for consumers who value the durability, patina, and heritage qualities of real leather but are increasingly aware of the environmental impacts and ethical concerns associated with both traditional livestock-based leather and some synthetic leather alternatives, which often rely on petrochemicals and lack biodegradability. A proposed expansion of the problem considers the lack of emotional connection and traceability in conventional materials, where the origin story of a leather good is typically one of anonymous industrial farming, creating a disconnect for consumers who seek meaningful, narrative-rich possessions.

## Solution / Product Overview

The project offers jewelry featuring inlays of cultivated leather grown from the donor cow's skin cells on a plant-based scaffold. The leather is produced in bioreactors and then vegetable-tanned, allowing the creators to present finished wearable pieces while asserting that no additional animal harvesting is required.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Real leather cultivated from living-animal skin cells grown on a plant-derived scaffold.
-   Inlays set within metal bezels and protected under a glass dome cabochon.
-   Options to choose hypoallergenic stainless steel or sterling silver for certain pieces.
-   Offered in multiple size, color, and material combinations.
-   Packaged in eco-friendly boxes cushioned with plant seed fiber used in the cultivation process.

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign speaks to people seeking animal-friendly, sustainable jewelry and those interested in owning a first-of-its-kind heirloom piece made from cultivated leather grown from a specific donor animal's cells.

## Development Status

The team shows finished jewelry inlays and describes past milestones: cells were isolated harmlessly in 2023, prototypes include a pendant and a card holder made in early 2025, and the leather is grown with patent-pending plant-based scaffolding. They state there are no outside approvals required and that the technology and cell lines are owned by the creators.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned actions include pilot testing to tune color and texture, inspecting scaffold density before use, preparing different concentrations of plant-based tanning ingredients, and securing jewelry settings after style counts are finalized at the end of the campaign. Production scaling will be addressed by adjusting modular cultivated-leather bioreactor technology and resources.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds support bringing the cultivated-leather jewelry to backers: producing inlays, performing pilot tests for consistency, and procuring jewelry settings and sustainable packaging to deliver finished pieces.

## Risks & Challenges

Stated risks include: loss of cryopreserved cells (mitigated by storage at multiple facilities); variability in final color and surface texture from vegetable tanning and scaffold differences (addressed through pilot testing and scaffold inspection); potential supply-chain changes requiring alternate jewelry settings of equal or better quality; and possible extended delivery times for later backers if demand is high.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by a founder with long-term tissue-engineering experience and cellular-agriculture leadership since 2018, who worked with a sanctuary and veterinary professionals to isolate the donor cells.

## What's Included

Jewelry pieces with cultivated-leather inlays (e.g., a rectangular inlay approximately的道 10 mm × 50 mm) and, for some items, a waxed linen cord; components are housed in metal bezels and glass cabochons.

## Technical Details

-   Plant-based scaffold from kapok seed fibers, needle-felted.
-   Surface treatment with plant-derived ingredients (e.g., sunflower lecithin, zein protein) to promote cell attachment.
-   Cells produce collagen that becomes vegetable-tanned leather.
-   Approximate inlay dimension: 10 mm × 50 mm.

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication. This challenge extends beyond establishing simple precedence to undermining trust in digital evidence within legal, journalistic, and commercial contexts, where the inability to definitively authenticate a file's provenance or creation time can have significant consequences.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
-   Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
-   Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
-   Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
-   Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Distinctiveness: Why This Approach Differs Meaningfully from Available Alternatives

This approach is distinct because it decouples the proof of existence from the file itself, anchoring only a hash to a public ledger, while most alternatives either require uploading the entire file to a centralized service or rely on complex, resource-intensive blockchain networks for storage and verification. The proposed system aims to provide a simpler, more accessible, and environmentally conscious verification layer that prioritizes user privacy and data sovereignty, avoiding the pitfalls of vendor lock-in or high transactional costs associated with many blockchain-based timestamping services.

## Revenue Logic

To sustain the venture, the team is planning to explore a tiered subscription model. The planned model would provide a free tier for infrequent, personal use, while offering paid tiers for professionals and businesses requiring higher-volume anchoring, advanced verification features, or dedicated support. This would allow the core service to remain broadly accessible while generating revenue from users who derive significant value from it.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets.
--- END PROJECT ---

## One-Sentence Summary

A lightweight, privacy-first tool that generates a verifiable fingerprint of a file and anchors it to a public, time-stamped ledger so anyone can prove originality and authenticity.

## Problem

The creators describe a digital landscape saturated with deepfakes, fake screenshots, copied artwork, and altered media, where "anyone can post anything," making it increasingly difficult to establish what's original or real. They frame the central question as how people can credibly prove ownership or first possession of digital work amid pervasive manipulation and duplication. This challenge extends beyond establishing simple precedence to undermining trust in digital evidence within legal, journalistic, and commercial contexts, where the inability to definitively authenticate a file's provenance or creation time can have significant consequences.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product creates a digital fingerprint of a user's file and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is presented as secure and privacy-preserving: users do not upload the actual file; instead, a compact fingerprint is used as a durable evidence marker. The creators position this as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that everyday people, as well as professionals, can rely on.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   File fingerprinting: produces a unique hash of a file for proof of originality.
-   Public, time-stamped anchoring: writes proof to a ledger that can be independently checked.
-   Privacy-first design: only hashed fingerprints are stored, not the underlying files.
-   Lightweight implementation: designed to be efficient and resource-conscious.
-   Security emphasis: presented as "lightweight, secure, and built for the future."

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out artists, small businesses, journalists, and anyone who wants to prove "I had this first." Primary uses include establishing authorship, deterring copycats, and documenting the creation time of digital assets.

## Development Status

The "core protocol already works," and an early form is live privately. The team is seeking to build a cleaner public interface and supporting infrastructure so the tool is usable by a broader audience.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned steps include hiring a developer and a designer to build a smoother public interface; polishing usability; and layering in infrastructure for scale. The team references a January beta target and says cushion time has been built into the schedule.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Funds will support building a public-facing site and the underlying infrastructure, along with the hiring needed to deliver a refined interface and broaden access.

## Risks & Challenges

The main risk is talent acquisition: delays in hiring or extended timelines could push back the January beta. Mitigations include existing architecture, a lean scope, added schedule buffer, and a commitment to communicate changes clearly.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by engineers who emphasize building for everyday creators in their lives. All architecture and content are created and reviewed by a human team.

## Technical Details

Only hashed fingerprints are stored, dramatically reducing storage and compute compared with systems that store full files or rely on energy-intensive consensus mechanisms. The goal is long-term security and transparency with minimal environmental impact.

## Distinctiveness: Why This Approach Differs Meaningfully from Available Alternatives

This approach is distinct because it decouples the proof of existence from the file itself, anchoring only a hash to a public ledger, while most alternatives either require uploading the entire file to a centralized service or rely on complex, resource-intensive blockchain networks for storage and verification. The proposed system aims to provide a simpler, more accessible, and environmentally conscious verification layer that prioritizes user privacy and data sovereignty, avoiding the pitfalls of vendor lock-in or high transactional costs associated with many blockchain-based timestamping services.

## Revenue Logic

To sustain the venture, the team is planning to explore a revenue model centered on a usage-based API. The planned model would provide a generous free tier for infrequent, personal use via a public web interface, while offering a paid API for developers, platforms, and businesses that need to programmatically anchor and verify large volumes of files. This would allow the core service to remain broadly accessible while generating revenue from integrations and high-volume use cases that derive significant value from automated, scalable verification.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises clear communication with backers if plans change and notes limited, supportive use of AI tools for coding and documentation; they are not building AI technology nor using AI to generate creative assets.

A specific, related challenge the venture plans to explore is the inefficiency and lack of standardization in the verification process for corporate matching gift programs, where employees often face cumbersome manual steps to prove their donations, creating friction that reduces participation. ## Target Users & Use Cases The venture plans to target both brands seeking to validate their supply chains and consumers looking for trustworthy ethical goods. A planned, specific target user group for initial outreach is procurement teams within consumer goods companies participating in sustainability certification or reporting programs, who need a streamlined way to discover vetted suppliers and provide indisputable proof of their ethical sourcing actions to qualify for certifications or meet regulatory requirements. The venture also plans to explore targeting non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and impact-focused philanthropic foundations as a distinct user group, who require independently verifiable, tamper-proof records of field-level sourcing events and material provenance to substantiate their impact reports to donors, auditors, and grant-making bodies. ## Solution / Product Overview The venture plans to build a tool that creates a digital fingerprint of a user's charitable event data—such as a donation receipt or a nonprofit's impact milestone—and records proof of that fingerprint on a public, time-stamped ledger. The approach is proposed to be secure and privacy-preserving: users would not upload sensitive raw data; instead, a compact fingerprint would serve as durable evidence. This is positioned as a quiet safeguard for digital truth that donors, nonprofits, and verifying partners can rely on. To increase trust, the team plans to explore adding a decentralized, community-run witness network to provide a secondary, distributed layer of attestation to the ledger's timestamps. Furthermore, the venture plans to explore the development of a simple, open-source verification widget that any third-party website (like a nonprofit's blog or a corporate social responsibility page) could embed to allow visitors to independently verify the timestamp and authenticity of a claimed charitable fingerprint directly from that page. Additionally, the venture plans to explore a feature where users could link multiple related fingerprints (e.g., a donation receipt, a supplier invoice, and a shipping confirmation) into a single, verifiable provenance bundle, creating a more comprehensive audit trail for complex ethical sourcing events. ## Delivery Model The venture plans a lightweight, privacy-first implementation. It would not store sensitive donor financial details or the underlying event files. Instead, it would generate compact, anonymized fingerprints of that data for ledger anchoring. The goal is a secure and resource-conscious design that maintains long-term verifiability with minimal infrastructure. The team plans to build a clean public interface and supporting infrastructure to make the verification tools usable by its target audience. ## Revenue Logic The venture plans to generate revenue through the sale of a subscription service to brands and suppliers for access to the verification ledger, advanced provenance reporting features, and supply chain management capabilities within the platform. An initial free trial period for the subscription service is proposed to onboard supplier and brand partners. The venture also plans to explore potential optional upgrades for enhanced connectivity or integration services for enterprise procurement or certification programs. ## Distinctiveness The venture aims to differentiate itself by offering heirloom-quality goods that merge immediate, tangible material qualities with enduring digital proof of ethical sourcing. Its proposed system does not just provide a product; it aims to create a permanent, independently verifiable record that the materials were sourced according to specific ethical standards at a specific time, addressing the credibility problem of sustainability claims. This focus on verifiable provenance from a specific, ethical source is presented as a unique safeguard for both consumer trust and material truth. The venture plans to explore a further point of differentiation: structuring its public ledger not just as a tamper-proof record, but as a machine-readable, open registry of ethical sourcing standards. This would allow the fingerprints to be programmatically linked to the precise definitions of the ethical standards they claim to uphold, aiming to create a new layer of semantic clarity and auditability that is missing from current provenance claims.
